1.w: The Beloved to Her Lover: I am a meadow flower from Sharon, a lily from the valleys. The Lover to His Beloved:

2.w: Like a lily among the thorns, so is my darling among the maidens. The Beloved about Her Lover:

3.w: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.

4.w: The Beloved about Her Lover: He brought me into the banquet hall, and he looked at me lovingly.

5.w: Sustain me with raisin cakes, refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.

6.w: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me. The Beloved to the Maidens:

7.w: I admonish you, O maidens of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and by the young does of the open fields: Do not awaken or arouse love until it pleases!

8.w: The Beloved about Her Lover: Listen! My lover is approaching! Look! Here he comes, leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills!

9.w: My lover is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look! There he stands behind our wall, gazing through the window, peering through the lattice.

10.w: The Lover to His Beloved: My lover spoke to me, saying: “Arise, my darling; My beautiful one, come away with me!

11.w: Look! The winter has passed, the winter rains are over and gone.

12.w: Blossoms have appeared in the land; the time for pruning and singing has come; the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.

13.w: The fig tree has ripened its figs; the vines have blossomed and give off their fragrance. Arise, come away my darling; my beautiful one, come away with me!”

14.w: The Lover to His Beloved: O my dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the mountain crags, let me see your face; let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.

15.w: The Beloved to Her Lover: Catch the foxes for us, the little foxes, that ruin the vineyards — for our vineyard is in bloom.

16.w: The Beloved about Her Lover: My lover is mine and I am his; he grazes among the lilies.

17.w: The Beloved to Her Lover: Until the dawn arrives and the shadows flee, turn, my beloved— be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountain gorges.
